item.title: FAQ
item.description:
How mature is the MYSQL module?

This pilot module targets simple, affordable MySQL clusters. Deployment convergence, HA failover, complete three-node outage recovery, replacement at the same address, daily physical backups, and monitoring/alerts have been systematically tested. Physical backup copy-back remains manual, with a runbook. It does not aim for PGSQL-level completeness: there is no PITR, DNS/HAProxy access layer, or online topology scaling. Local Router and the NODE Layer 2 VIP are supported. Validate the module against your requirements and rehearse recovery before production use.

item.title: Metrics
item.description:
MYSQL metrics come from mysqld_exporter (mysql_ raw metrics), node_exporter backup textfiles (/var/lib/node_exporter/textfile/mysql.prom), and vmalert recording rules (mysql:ins:* / mysql:cls:*). Dashboards and alerts primarily use recording rules; this page is their complete dictionary.

files/victoria/rules/mysql.yml provides 70 module recording rules, all listed here. mysql_exporter_up = up{job="mysql"} additionally comes from Infra’s shared liveness recording rules. These recorded metrics do not appear at the raw mysqld_exporter endpoint. mysql_up is the exporter’s database connection probe result.

item.title: Monitoring
item.description:
MYSQL uses Pigsty’s observability stack: mysqld_exporter and node_exporter textfiles feed VictoriaMetrics, Journald/Vector send error logs to VictoriaLogs, Grafana provides 5 dashboards, and vmalert loads 70 recording rules and 8 actionable alerts.

Collection Architecture

Each MySQL node runs mysqld_exporter on 9104, collecting server and MGR metrics with the least-privilege dbuser_monitor@'127.0.0.1' account. mysql-backup also writes the local physical backup timestamp and size to /var/lib/node_exporter/textfile/mysql.prom; node_exporter reports these, and rules join them to cluster metrics by ip. item.title: Playbook
item.description:
mysql.yml deploys and adjusts clusters to declared state. Separate mysql-rm.yml retires members or clusters with safeguards. Before every removal, recheck the target, backups, and exact confirmation value.

Selected clusters follow check → install → bootstrap → access → provision → backup → monitor:

./mysql.yml -l my-test --check # preflight: validate declarations against the live state
./mysql.yml -l my-test # converge one cluster (must select all members)

item.title: Administration
item.description:
This page covers daily MYSQL operations. Declare state in the inventory and converge it with playbooks. Rerunning ./mysql.yml -l <cluster> recovers an offline member, a complete outage with all three hosts reachable, or a dead member replaced at the same IP. Physical backup copy-back and incomplete outages with fewer than three reachable hosts require the manual procedures below.

Quick Reference

Operation Command
Deploy / converge / recover a cluster ./mysql.yml -l <cluster>
Preflight without changes ./mysql.yml -l <cluster> --check
Local root client shortcut my (equivalent to sudo mysql --defaults-extra-file=/etc/mysql/pigsty/root.cnf)
AdminAPI cluster status (HA) mysh (prints dba.getCluster().status() by default)
Inspect MGR topology my -e "SELECT MEMBER_HOST,MEMBER_STATE,MEMBER_ROLE FROM performance_schema.replication_group_members;"
Trigger a backup sudo systemctl start mysql-backup (only the writable primary executes it in HA)
Remove and destroy one member ./mysql-rm.yml -l <IP> -e mysql_safeguard=false (automatically switches primary first if needed)
Stop a cluster while retaining data ./mysql-rm.yml -l <cluster> -e mysql_safeguard=false -e mysql_rm_data=false
Destroy the entire cluster ./mysql-rm.yml -l <cluster> -e mysql_safeguard=false (always retains the backup directory)

Status Checks and Shortcuts

Installation deploys /etc/profile.d/mysql.sh, which provides my for all topologies and mysh on HA nodes. Credentials are stored under /etc/mysql/pigsty/ and readable only by root. Examples use EL; on Debian/Ubuntu the MySQL service unit is mysql, not mysqld.

item.title: Parameters
item.description:
The MYSQL deployment role exposes 13 parameters; the removal role adds 3 protected operational parameters, for 16 total. Versions, ports, character set, TLS paths, and timer schedules are fixed by the role. Memory defaults follow node resources and PostgreSQL colocation. Use mysql_parameters to adjust server behavior.

Quick Reference

Parameter Level Default Description
mysql_cluster Cluster required Cluster name and identity
mysql_seq Instance required 1 for standalone; sequential 1..3 for HA
mysql_root_password Cluster DBUser.Root Local root password
mysql_monitor_password Cluster DBUser.Monitor Exporter identity password
mysql_cluster_password Cluster DBUser.Cluster AdminAPI/Router/backup identity password
mysql_databases Cluster [] Additive database declarations
mysql_users Cluster [] Additive user and grant declarations
mysql_parameters Cluster/Instance {} [mysqld] option overrides
mysql_data Cluster/Instance /data/mysql MySQL data directory, including binlog/ and tmp/
mysql_backup_enabled Cluster true Daily full-backup timer
mysql_backup_dir Cluster /data/backups/mysql Local physical backup root
mysql_backup_retention Cluster 3 Number of local full backups to retain
mysql_exporter_enabled Cluster true Exporter and monitoring target

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
Declare the cluster in inventory. mysql.yml adjusts live state to match. This page covers topology and configuration blocks. See Parameters for the full reference.

Before You Deploy

  • Manage nodes with NODE. Install the shared CA at /etc/pki/ca.crt through node_ca. MYSQL issues leaf certificates only.
  • Include mysql in repositories with node_repo_modules: node,infra,mysql, or cache packages locally with repo_extra_packages: [mysql].
  • Use supported platforms: x86_64 EL 8/9/10, Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 22/24; or aarch64 EL 9/10.
  • Replace all three platform passwords (mysql_root_password, mysql_monitor_password, mysql_cluster_password) with production values. Preflight rejects CHANGE_ME prefixes and INI interpolation expressions of the form %(...)s in mysql_monitor_password.

item.title: Module: MYSQL
item.description:
MySQL is a widely used open-source relational database. Pigsty’s MYSQL module installs a fixed native MySQL 8.4 LTS platform on managed nodes. Choose a standalone instance or three-node single-primary InnoDB Cluster with Group Replication. The module manages TLS, backups, monitoring, and lifecycle.

Current status: Pilot module

MYSQL is a supplementary pilot module for a simple, low-cost MySQL cluster. Its scope is smaller than PGSQL. Core capabilities have been systematically tested: deployment convergence, HA failover, recovery after a complete three-node outage, replacement at the same address, daily backups, and monitoring/alerts. Destructive procedures such as physical backup copy-back remain manual operations. See the runbooks under Administration.
